## Sandbox Profiles

The Who can see what card is a small grid, so each run's reach is seen at a glance: the project's areas down its left, and the modes across its top, Code, Spec, Ask, and Freeform, each in its mode's colour. Each cell is a small label: "Edit", on a faint tint of the theme's success colour; "Read", on a faint tint of its accent; or "No access", muted and untinted. Hovering a cell shows the paths it covers. Beneath the grid, one muted line says what every mode can reach outside the project, as "System and toolchains read only; the harness's folders, build caches, and a temporary folder editable". The grid follows the classification and the Spec tasks switches as they change, so a change shows at once what it allows.
The grid is editable, for the open project: clicking a cell opens a small menu beneath it of Edit, Read, and No access, the cell's level ticked, and picking one sets it, the cell changing at once and the project's profiles following, as the [Sandbox](../sandbox/index.md#sandbox) says. Each cell the user has set is marked with a small dot in its corner, and its menu has "Use default" too, which puts back what the profile gives it by default. Only what the sandbox can enforce is offered: a choice that would let a Code run read the spec source, or a Spec run change the code, is shown disabled in its menu, its tooltip saying the separation of code and spec is never relaxed, and Ask can never be given Edit anywhere; what else each area allows is as its areas say. A "Reset grid" button beneath the grid, enabled while any cell is set, puts every cell back to its default. Each change is saved to `.suspense/sandbox.json` straight away and takes effect from the next run. Setting the Code row to Read in the Spec column is the same as the Spec tasks card's "Read the code" switch, and setting Other files to Read there the same as "Read the whole project", so the switches and the grid always agree.

## Sandbox Areas

Each area is a row of the grid, its name at its left and beneath it, muted and cut off with an ellipsis, what it covers, its folders and patterns as written, as `src/, tests/` or `**/*.pi`, the whole list in its tooltip, so what a row means is never a guess. The areas are these, in this order.
- Code, the code roots and patterns of the Code and spec card
- Spec source, the spec roots and patterns of that card
- Compiled reference, the harness directory's reference folder, as `.claude/reference`
- Suspense data, the project's `.suspense` folder, where Suspense keeps the project's history, queue, prompts, and settings, as the ProjectData says
- each area the user has added, in the order added
- Other files, everything in the project none of the areas above covers, such as a README, build files, and scripts, listed as the top-level files and folders it holds, as `README.md, Cargo.toml, scripts/`
An area can be added with "Add area" beneath the grid: a row to type its name into, as "Docs" or "Assets", and then its folders and patterns, chosen with the folder browser or typed, as the Code and spec card adds them. Each added area has its own levels in each mode, set as any cell is, starting at what Other files has, and is taken out of Other files. Clicking an added area's name lets it be renamed, its covered line lets its folders and patterns be edited, and a remove button at its right, shown on hover, removes it, its files going back into Other files. Code and Spec source are edited in the Code and spec card, and Compiled reference and Suspense data can't be changed in what they cover, only in their levels. An added area may not cover anything classed as code or spec, nor the reference or Suspense data: such a folder or pattern is marked in the theme's error colour, saying which area already has it.
Suspense data can be given Edit only in Freeform, and is No access in every other mode by default, but for the files a run is given on their own, as its understanding file, which the grid notes beneath the row. Other files and every added area can be given any level in every mode but Ask, which can only Read.

## Sandbox Classification
## Classification

Which paths are code and which are spec is the project's to say, in `.suspense/sandbox.json`, saved with its data, as the [ProjectData](../project-data/index.md#project-data) says, and edited in the [SettingsWindow](../settings-window/index.md#settings-window)'s Sandbox section. It holds a list of code roots and a list of spec roots, each a path in the project, and patterns classing files anywhere as code or spec, as `**/*.pi` for spec, so a project laid out in any way, with several roots, or spec and code side by side, can be classed. With no file, the project's code location is its only code root and its spec location its only spec root, as the [ProjectLocations](../project-locations/index.md#project-locations) says. A path classed as both is a contradiction, and runs refuse until it is resolved; a path classed as neither is denied to Code and Spec runs alike, and readable by questions. The profiles are built from the classification each time a run starts, so a change takes effect from the next run.
The same file holds the project's own levels for each profile, as set in the [SettingsWindow](../settings-window/index.md#settings-window)'s grid: for each mode and each area of the project, code, spec source, compiled reference, Suspense data, any area the user has added, each a name with its folders and patterns, and other files, everything none of those covers, Edit, Read, or No access, where it differs from the profile's default. An added area may not overlap code, spec, the reference, Suspense data, or another added area; one that does is a contradiction. The levels are applied over the defaults when the profile is built, and never past what the sandbox allows: a level that would let a Code run read the spec's source, a Spec run change the code, a Question run change anything, or any run but Freeform change Suspense data, is refused when the policy is compiled, as a contradiction, and the run doesn't start until it is put right.

content.text:
The grid's rows now say what they cover, the two vague rows are renamed, and you can add your own areas. The build is clean, and all 21 sandbox and settings tests pass. As before, that was in a copy of the code, because this session's sandbox blocks files Suspense's build needs.

- **Every row shows what it covers:** a muted line under each name lists its folders and patterns, such as `src/` or `**/*.pi`, with the full list in its tooltip.
- **"Project data" is now "Suspense data":** it's the `.suspense/` folder. By default it shows No access in every mode, with a note that each run still gets its own files there (its understanding file and the fluency files). Only Freeform can be given Edit.
- **"Everything else" is now "Other files":** it lists what it actually holds at the top level, such as `README.md, Cargo.toml, scripts/`.
- **Your own areas:** "Add area" beneath the grid asks for a name, then opens a row where you add folders (with the folder browser) and patterns.
  - It starts with Other files' levels until you set its own, and its files come out of Other files.
  - Click its name to rename it, click its covered line to edit its folders and patterns, and use the button that appears on hover to remove it.
- **Overlaps:** a folder or pattern that another area already covers is shown in red with "already in …". An overlapping area stops every run until it's fixed.
- **Levels:** Other files and added areas can be set to any level, except that Ask can only read. The code and spec separation is unchanged.
- **Saving:** areas are saved in `sandbox.json` with their own levels. "Reset grid" clears every level, including the added areas'.

As last time, the menu shows the reasons for greyed-out choices as plain lines, because its items can't have tooltips.
